title: WYGWYL 14-Poem Suite — Definitive Director's Cut Film Assembly
author: Mark Anthony Thomas

suites.title: OUT OF LIFE
suites.full_verse: What we've made, we don't want. What we've sold — to the world, to ourselves — doesn't exist. I look for a way out: through the hallways, within the drawers, and fire escapes. The vape gathers, inside and out. My vision blurs. I move toward the window — and you only get further away. More haze. What isn't mine, I still can not give.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Definitive 26-second wide master establishing the domestic stasis of the dim teal bedroom with vinyl records on wall and rainy window overlooking black car.

suites.title: FLASHING LIGHTS
suites.full_verse: It was the type of silent scream a trapped lover makes to escape: a pending marriage, a concussion, a set of walls caving inward. An emergency call while tossing and turning — the silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight, to digest a truth. A truth he could neither alter nor change. What isn't mine, I still can not give.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Frantic sprint down monochrome orange subway stairs to breach transit threshold and escape marital confinement.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: It was the type of silent scream a trapped lover makes to escape...

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Shadowed stylist on night street corner wrapped in glowing crimson plasma mist reflecting internal emergency call.

suites.title: HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT
suites.full_verse: Ode to forever — a tambourine sounds off an empty temple, empty choir stands, empty prayer lines. And abandoned baptism pools. It flies in through the rose window — still whole. A broken promise.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Man standing in twilight ocean surf releasing brilliant glowing red heart ribbons that coil across his chest and drift into the sea breeze.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Ode to forever... It flies in through the rose window — still whole.

suites.title: NEVERMORE
suites.full_verse: What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore — and the ashes of expired wildfires cover sands, and debris lifted from the night sea water's floor. The waves calm to folded whispers; the winds mute the trees. The right level of silence, to find a throbbing heart — it used to be mine. I lift it with care: nevermore.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: POET in sunglasses standing centered in parched cathedral churchyard as dark ravens glide closely past his shoulders in golden atmospheric haze.

suites.title: BLOODLINES
suites.full_verse: Now go, they tell me. To ask if I can inherit the earth — to ask if I can name my own stars. Even galaxies, if I may. The past, too, was waiting for me — coming of age in the shared rooms of humid basements as bedrooms; mattress pads where the wood beams of Southern pine could comfort my spine. It didn't. To dream was to prevail.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: POET with arms open in center-axis street, chest cavity displaying glowing white skeleton and beating red heart pulsating with bright energy.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: To dream was to prevail... Ask if I can name my own stars.

suites.title: RESURRECTING ATLANTIS
suites.full_verse: Poets, who eased generations down yellow brick roads — and plucked our souls out of their secret places, to follow comets to the capital city of our collective consciousness. Resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one — the pact we've made here with nature, abandoned and hoped for the best, back on life.

suites.title: DJ TURN ME UP
suites.full_verse: DJ, turn me up, please. Eyes wide shut, chin nested at the arch of the weight of these spoken words. I have a love story to tell — of ghosts, whispering unfolded dilutions, birthed in purity, and dying in the vineyards of sun-soaked evergreen fields, unnourished.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Young Black boy in bright red hoodie resting cheek on arm at roadside diner window, gazing thoughtfully through raindrops at overcast highway.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: I have a love story to tell — of ghosts, whispering unfolded dilutions...

suites.title: NEWLY SINGLE
suites.full_verse: Pulsing, and head throbbing from the music — and empty, on a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations. The soul escapes my body, and leaves him on the dance floor — just flesh and bones. Rejection and heartache hit different, with no feelings afloat.

curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: The soul escapes my body, and leaves him on the dance floor — just flesh and bones.

curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Rejection and heartache hit different, with no feelings afloat.

suites.title: YET, HEARD
suites.full_verse: Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it. We talk for years, travel through time — we grow old together, I believe. Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she's never known. Before I go, I call on my father — his calming demeanor summoned from the yonders. We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken. Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: POET leaps off industrial rooftop ledge into steam, camera flips upward as he glides through radiant sunlit clouds wearing sunglasses toward the lens.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Before I go... Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: POET in black beanie and hoodie seated on brick roof ledge facing away from camera watching massive white plumes of steam surge into overcast sky.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she's never known.

suites.title: MAGIC RIDE
suites.full_verse: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are — blissful, and oddly sensitive. I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings, and hop on. Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell — being everywhere, with no one to love. I let the noise block the noise. The way I ride: eyes turn, heads twist — and prove the magic still exists. The moon settles, and I can see a morning ahead for me.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Coastal highway at twilight lined with tall palm silhouettes, headlights and streetlamps smearing into horizontal golden light streaks.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: I let the noise block the noise. The way I ride: eyes turn, heads twist — and prove the magic still exists.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Forward-tracking coastal vehicle perspective accelerating along seaside asphalt into dawn.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: The moon settles, and the tease of distant stars subsides — and I can see a morning ahead for me.

suites.title: NEW DAY
suites.full_verse: Fog covers the seas and hugs the tree-covered hills, floating through the morning as it exhales its introduction. This world is at peace. In the awakening of dawn, in fresh muted colors: we can rebuild this temple. It's a new day — a catharsis for me to say, with newfound energies and recycled airs. Edgeless dreams that reflect the skies... that we too can walk on water.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: POET in dark jacket and sunglasses wading waist-deep through dense blooming sea of thousands of yellow chrysanthemums filling an ancient stone library.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: In the awakening of dawn, in fresh muted colors: we can rebuild this temple. It's a new day — a catharsis...

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Solitary pilgrim in dark robes walking thoughtfully through tall golden grass in grand sunlit ruined cathedral colonnade.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: We can rebuild this temple — under vibrant sun rays of glory...

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Saffron-robed Buddhist monks on ancient stone temple steps in radiant morning sunlight and prismatic refractions.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: And of modern faiths — that we too can walk on water.

suites.title: REUNION
suites.full_verse: Decades later, there is less time for words, and more space for laughter — hugs with no reason, and loud voices, so our hearts can be overheard. Reflecting on legacies, and creeds once told — of elders, now past. Or will we make time, in the sands of burning hourglasses? Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: Two kin women sharing an intimate, radiant laugh over a phone in golden chandelier bokeh, celebrating family survival.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Decades later, there is less time for words, and more space for laughter — hugs with no reason, and loud voices...

curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.

suites.title: HOW TO WIN MY HEART
suites.full_verse: Find me at the harbor, at the small tables, watching. The couples orbit each other the way Jupiter keeps its moons — close, and counted. Life has burned all my love stories — victory-less seasons. So I harvest the flowers instead — scarlet poppies, purple blossoms — and they become my power. Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello. Don't make me leave. I escaped here for a reason.

curated_shots.editorial_reason: POET in black tracksuit with clear plastic sleeves and dark sunglasses walking forward with stepped multi-exposure after-image trail.
curated_shots.matched_verse_phrase: Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello.

suites.title: HOT MINUTE
suites.full_verse: A hot minute. The haze gathers on the water — and everything I built here learns to be weather: the city, the temple, the harbor. It takes me last, and from the ground up. I am reluctant — but I have been weather before. All black again. But no walls this time. A life flashes the way a reel does: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars, the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass. Our dance together is a victory. An old door, from a vintage somewhere. It opens on a slow party — the kind I once fell out of a window to escape. This time, I choose the door.
